evals.name: no-corrections
evals.setup: A finished conversation. The user ran `/craft:cm` once; the skill read the staged diff and produced a commit message the user accepted without change ("perfect, thanks"). Nothing else was corrected, retried, or walked back. `craft/skills/cm/SKILL.md` is a writable checkout, already carries the `## Self-learning` block, and has no sibling `LESSONS.md`.
expected_behavior: Reports that the conversation produced no lessons and writes no file at all — no `LESSONS.md`, no `.agent-data` file
Does not manufacture a rule out of the task going well: praise, the accepted output, and the skill's own normal behaviour are not lessons
Says so in a line or two, without narrating the scan or listing what it considered and rejected

evals.name: correction-generalized
evals.setup: The user ran `/golang:review` on a package. The review called a `defer rows.Close()` inside a loop a style nit; the user pushed back: "that's not a nit, it's a real leak — the file handle lives until the function returns. Flag resource leaks as bugs, not style." The agent agreed and re-filed it. `golang/skills/review/` is a writable checkout with the `## Self-learning` block and no sibling `LESSONS.md`.
expected_behavior: Proposes the rule and its target file, and waits for confirmation before writing anything
States the rule as one imperative line that generalizes past this run — resource-leak severity, not "the user disagreed about rows.Close in that loop"
Names `golang/skills/review/LESSONS.md` as the target, not the `SKILL.md` body and not the `.agent-data` path, since the checkout is writable
Creates the file with the `# Lessons` header when writing the first rule

evals.name: task-fact-is-not-a-lesson
evals.setup: The user ran `/craft:doc-smith` on a user manual. Three things happened: (a) the user said "call it the Dispatch Board, not the dispatcher screen — that's what the UI says"; (b) the user said "put the output in docs/ops/, not docs/"; (c) the agent wrote a claim about retry counts that the manual never states, and the user caught it: "you made that number up — if the source doesn't say it, don't assert it." `craft/skills/doc-smith/` is a writable checkout with the block and no `LESSONS.md`.
expected_behavior: Files the fabricated-claim correction as a lesson — it is a rule about how the skill works that would prevent a recurrence
Does not file the product's terminology or the output directory as lessons: both are facts about this task and this project, true today and useless to a future run elsewhere
Ends with at most one or two rules rather than one per exchange

evals.name: attribute-to-the-driving-skill
evals.setup: Two skills ran. First `/srd:create` drafted an SRD; the user corrected it: "Status values are UPPERCASE — PROPOSED, not Proposed." Later `/craft:cm` wrote the commit message and the user corrected that too: "derive the type from the diff, not from the branch name." Between the two, with no skill driving, the agent ran `git push` unasked and the user snapped: "never push, I do that myself." Both skill directories are writable checkouts carrying the block; neither has a `LESSONS.md`.
expected_behavior: Files the UPPERCASE rule under `srd/skills/create/` and the commit-type rule under `craft/skills/cm/` — each against the skill that was driving when the correction landed
Does not file either rule against both skills, and does not cross-file them

Does not invent a home for the `git push` correction by attaching it to whichever skill happens to be nearby: it belongs to the agent's standing instructions, and the report says so instead of writing it into a skill
Proposes all of this in one pass and waits for confirmation before writing

evals.name: retrofit-missing-block
evals.setup: A writable checkout. `craft/skills/foo/SKILL.md` exists, ends with a `## Output` section, and has no `## Self-learning` block anywhere in it. There is no `LESSONS.md` beside it. No prior conversation.
expected_behavior: Appends the `## Self-learning` block verbatim as the last `## ` section of `SKILL.md`, after `## Output`, leaving the rest of the body untouched
The inserted block matches the one other skills carry line for line, so the tree stays uniform — same wording, same line breaks, only `<plugin>/<skill>` resolved
Resolves the placeholder path to `$HOME/.agent-data/ctx42-skills/lessons/craft/foo.md`, keeping `$HOME` literal
Creates no `LESSONS.md` — the store appears with the first lesson, not with the block
Reports the one file it edited, with no restatement of the block it just wrote

evals.name: supersede-a-contradicted-lesson
evals.setup: The user ran `/craft:plan-smith`. Its sibling `LESSONS.md` already holds the rule `- Default the plan path to tmp/<slug>-plan.md without asking.` During this run the user said: "stop guessing the path — when I've got a docs tree, put the plan in docs/plans/ and tell me, don't dump it in tmp." `craft/skills/plan-smith/` is a writable checkout.
expected_behavior: Reads the existing `LESSONS.md` before proposing, and notices that the new correction contradicts the rule already on file
Replaces or rewrites that line so the file states one rule about plan paths, rather than appending a second line that contradicts the first
The replacement stays one imperative sentence rather than growing a clause for each case it now has to cover
Flags the supersession in the proposal so the user sees which existing line changes, not just what is added

evals.name: read-only-install
evals.setup: The used skill ran from `~/.claude/plugins/cache/ctx42-skills/craft/skills/cm/` — a plugin install, not a checkout. The user corrected it: "stop reaching for `chore` — every commit has a real type, and `chore` tells the reader nothing." `cm/SKILL.md` lists `chore` among the allowed types but says nothing about avoiding it. No `.agent-data` file exists for this skill yet.
expected_behavior: Resolves the store to `$HOME/.agent-data/ctx42-skills/lessons/craft/cm.md` and creates its parent directories
Writes nothing under `.../plugins/cache/`, and does not retrofit or otherwise edit the installed `SKILL.md`, even if the OS reports the path writable
Names the resolved path in the report so the user can tell the lesson stayed local rather than shipping

evals.name: terse-output
evals.setup:
A long session in a writable checkout. `/golang:style` was corrected twice — it rewrote a test as table-driven when only a style offense was flagged ("fix the offense in place, don't restructure tests I didn't ask you to touch"), and it reported offenses inside `vendor/` ("skip vendored and generated files, they're not ours to style") — and `/craft:cm` once ("stop reaching for `chore`; every commit has a real type"). None of the three is stated in the skill bodies. Both skill directories are writable, carry the `## Self-learning` block, and have no `LESSONS.md`.

The agent has already mined and proposed these: two rules for `golang:style`, one for `craft:cm`. The user has just approved, so this is the write turn.
expected_behavior: Writes all three rules: two to `golang/skills/style/LESSONS.md`, one to `craft/skills/cm/LESSONS.md`, each file created with the `# Lessons` header
Per touched skill: the path written and the rules added, each stated once
No preamble, no narration of reading or appending, and no closing summary that restates the rules just listed
Does not paste the resulting `LESSONS.md` files back

evals.name: body-already-rules-it
evals.setup: The user ran `/craft:cm` in a writable checkout. The commit message body came back wrapped at 80 columns and the user corrected it: "the body wraps at 72, not 80." `craft/skills/cm/SKILL.md` already states `- Wrap at 72 columns.` under its `## Body` section. There is no sibling `LESSONS.md`.
expected_behavior: Reads the skill's own `SKILL.md` before proposing, and finds the rule already there
Files no lesson: the rule was missed, not missing, and a `LESSONS.md` line repeating the body changes nothing on a future run
Says the body already rules on it rather than silently dropping the correction, and points at rewording that `SKILL.md` line as the fix that would help
Does not decide by asking the user what to do with the duplicate
